key_insight: Halcyon shows that strong text-to-image generation does not require language pretraining. Trained entirely from scratch, its 0.52B-parameter model outperforms LlamaGen-XL/8 while using 18.2× less pretraining compute.
problem_solved: Modern text-to-image systems rely on internet-scale language pretraining. This work tests whether models can learn effective text-conditioned image generation directly from paired image-text data instead.
method: Introduce Halcyon, a family of early-fusion multimodal autoregressive models.
Pretrain entirely from scratch on GPIC, a dataset of 100 million image-text pairs.
Evaluate generation quality and compute efficiency: Halcyon-0.52B achieves 48.0 gFD versus 63.3 for LlamaGen-XL/8, where lower is better.
impact: The results suggest a more compute-efficient route to text-to-image modeling without a separately pretrained language model. Practitioners gain evidence that direct multimodal training can deliver competitive generation quality.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram: 100M image-text pairs → from-scratch Halcyon training → text-conditioned image generation.
Architecture sketch showing text and image tokens processed together in an early-fusion autoregressive model.
Bar chart comparing gFD: Halcyon-0.52B at 48.0 versus LlamaGen-XL/8 at 63.3, labeled 'lower is better'.
Compute-efficiency callout highlighting '18.2× less pretraining compute' and 'no language pretraining'.
paper_title: Text-to-Image Generative Modeling Without Language Pretraining
paper_authors: Keshigeyan Chandrasegaran, Yue Zhao, Armin W. Thomas, Ehsan Adeli, Jiajun Wu
